title: One selector controls one local height-error direction
statement: With H_i=[(Q a_i) cross u_i]/u_i,z, delta_h=H delta_phi. All nine introduced H are invertible. Selector tangent v=dh/dtheta can correct only span(H^-1 v); two angular directions remain locally uncontrolled, or three on a flat land v=0. A separate illustrative quintic transition gives a 1 um error perpendicular to the control direction, leaving .00263362 degrees; flat-land (1,-1,1) um gives .00634115 degrees. This is a restricted first-order diagnostic, not a general one-input impossibility or producer-track reconstruction.
